steps: Status epilepticus: protect airway, O2, glucose; IV lorazepam (or IM midazolam), repeat once.
Second-line: IV levetiracetam, valproate or phenytoin/fosphenytoin.
Refractory status → ICU, intubation, anaesthetic infusion (propofol/midazolam).
Correct provoking causes (hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, alcohol, drugs, infection).
First unprovoked seizure: usually no drug; start AED if high recurrence risk / abnormal EEG-MRI; neurology referral, driving advice.

drugRefs.dose: 4 mg IV, repeat once after 5–10 min if seizure continues
drugRefs.why: First-line abortive therapy for status epilepticus. If no IV access, use IM midazolam.
Alternative first-line when IV access is not immediately available.
Second-line control after benzodiazepines; well tolerated with few interactions.
Alternative second-line agent; avoid in pregnancy and hepatic disease.

drugRefs.dose: phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV (fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg) at ≤50 mg/min with cardiac monitoring
drugRefs.why: Alternative second-line; requires cardiac/BP monitoring during loading.
For refractory status epilepticus requiring intubation and burst-suppression; midazolam infusion is an alternative.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Seizures and Epilepsy
American Epilepsy Society — Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus

decision.label: Status epilepticus: benzodiazepine first, then 2nd-line AED

confirm: Stereotyped paroxysmal event ± post-ictal confusion. First seizure vs known epilepsy; status if >5 min or recurrent without recovery.
